text:
Few forwards in the league have less to show for their work right now than Alex Laferriere. The Kings winger has 4 goals on 9.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a 6.3% shooting rate against a league norm of 13.4%. His teammates are snakebitten too: Los Angeles has scored 6.2 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice.

The process says he belongs. He's playing 19:26 a night, up from 18:19, and he's on the ice for 73% of the Kings' power-play chances after 30% last season. At five on five, the Kings take 58% of the expected goals with him out there, 11 points better than without him. He's also throwing his weight around, with 63 hits in 20 games.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him at 0.9 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense, and the third-round pick out of Harvard has kept climbing since. Our numbers flag him as due: the looks keep coming, and goals tend to follow chances. Watch the shooting percentage, not the point total.
